findings.title: The Regency Of Algiers
findings.description: The Regency of Algiers: Patterns of Power (1516–1830) is an analytical case study examining how an order of power was founded, dressed, and held across three centuries . The study follows the state's trajectory from the seizure of Algiers by the corsair brothers Aruj and Khayr al-Din , through its submission to the Ottoman sultan and the eventual rise of the janissary corporation , to the capitulation of the Kasba to a French army on July 5, 1830 . Relying on primary administrative records, consular testimonies, eyewitness accounts, and period inscriptions , the work investigates an order whose revenue ran through maritime and state chokepoints , governed by a corporation that recruited free adult volunteers abroad while barring native Algerians from its pay registers and highest ranks . The volume explores the mechanics of an institutional arrangement where individual titles—such as places on the pay register, prize shares, and farmed offices—were strictly non-heritable and died with their holders , yet the corporate system itself endured . Rather than treating the Regency simply through the conventional lens of a "pirate state," the study details its administrative realities: the extraction of surplus via monopolies, tribute, and escheat ; the dual claims of holy war and diplomatic treaty under Ottoman safe-conduct ; the complete separation between local religious formation and state governance ; and the structural forces that eventually hollowed the order prior to the 1830 conquest .

findings.title: Pirates of Barbary : corsairs, conquests, and captivity in the seventeenth-century Mediterranean
description: It's easy to think of piracy as a romantic way of life long gone--if not for today's headlines of robbery and kidnapping on the high seas. Pirates have existed since the invention of commerce itself, but they reached the zenith of their power during the 1600s, when the Mediterranean was the crossroads of the world, and pirates were the scourge of Europe and the glory of Islam. They attacked ships, enslaved crews, plundered cargoes, enraged governments, and swayed empires. Historian Adrian Tinniswood brings alive this chapter in history, where clashes between pirates of the East--Tunis, Algiers, and Tripoli--and governments of the West--England, France, Spain, and Venice--grew increasingly intense and dangerous, and he shows how their maneuverings between the Muslim empires and Christian Europe shed light on the religious and moral battles that still rage today.--From publisher description
Includes bibliographical references (p. [325]-333) and index

findings.description: Biography of Jan Jansen van Haarlem (c1585-c1640) and his son Anthony Jansen van Salee (1609-c1680). Jan Jansen, a Dutch merchant, became a corsair in Algiers and Sallee (Morocco) before becoming Governor of Oualida, Morocco under Sultan al-Walid. His son Anthony emigrated to New Amsterdam, arriving with his wife Grietje Reyniers, in 1630.

description: xviii, 304 pages ; 25 cm

Indonesia receives offers of textiles. Earthquake. West Indies 114 for 3. Bomb outrages in Algiers. MONTY: TRUE CHINESE GOVT IS IN PEKING. NOT IN UN. GREAT FUTURE. 'Inspector' John Wallace does it again. Chemical plant explosion kills four. CALLING ALL TEENAGERS! Start sending now! Call for African Union. NKRUMAH PROPOSES CONFERENCE TO FORM NEW U.S.A. HISTORIC DUTY. Ireland extends coastal waters. Demonstrations planned in UK. SOS message investigated. Australian for Palace. Reward offered for return of infant child. SEVERE COLD. Historical documents traced. Arctic mishap did not endanger team of scientists. Formation of single Commonwealth office suggested. TRIPLE FUNCTION. 'Sea monster' is washed ashore. Subway system. FLAT HEAD. Subway system. Prospectors keep an eye on flowers. The world of science. Golden boughs. The future. Are ambassadors really necessary? Everyone knows. All he does. Odd thing. The answer. So harmful. Wild dream. PRACTICAL HOMECRAFT. FUR AT ANY PRICE. By PEGGY MASSIN, Reuter's Corresponden.t A HELEN BURKE RECIPE. Walnut Cake. A WORD WITH THE DOCTOR ON THE TROT. TASTY TIPS. JUST PEACHY. QUICK SUDAE. EXCELLENT SEASONING. Dirty Pant. Shell Fish. Hygiens. BY ONE OF LONDON'S MOST CONTROVERSIAL VOICES... Iadmit it frankly -here the Church has failed. Unprepared. BY DR. MERVYN STOCKWOOD. Could not read. Easy to forget. Indifferent. The harvests. Taipan's Rugby match today. H.R. CLELLAND GIVEN HONOUR TO FIELD XV AGAINST CBF'F TEAM. A battle royal. Odds on Taipan's XV. Much stronger. The teams. Only change of rules can prevent tennis from being a crash-bang affair. By DEREK JOHN. FIRST TEST MATCH-ENGLAND SCORE 482. West Indies Iose 3 wickets. 17 months jail for saying 'Heil Hitler'. Knock up 114 runs before close of play. Night-watchmen. No-ball incident. Plumb pitch. First bowl. Golfer equals course record. BRITISH TENNIS PLAYER REACHES SEMI-FINALS. BRIGHT CENTURY BY POLICEMAN. Asian Basketball Championship. SURRENDER DOCUMENT STOLEN FROM MUSEUM.

catalogue_leads.context_excerpt: "Comment redécouvrir le monde méditerranéen loin des clichés fabriqués et des images attendues ? Un monde en noir et bleu. Le noir de Goya, des désastres de la guerre, de la mafia et des années noires à Beyrouth, Sarajevo, Alger ou Jérusalem. Le bleu de Miré, celui des Lumières et des poètes, du "Grand Tour" et des villes cosmopolites telles Istanbul ou Alexandrie. Ce livre met en scène tant les représentations que les visions qui composent le rêve méditerranéen un rêve pluriel, restitué à partir des deux rives

catalogue_leads.context_excerpt: eux parties, il donne d'abord à voir 150 oeuvres du XVIIIe siècle à aujourd'hui: peintures, dessins, manuscrits, photographies, installations. Un abécédaire thématique, composé par les meilleurs spécialistes et amoureux de la Méditerranée prolonge ce voyage en près de 50 étapes: A comme Alger en 1830, C comme cosmopolitisme, M comme Marseille en 1943, 0 comme orientalisme... Entre contemplation et analyse, cet ouvrage associe plaisir du texte, originalité des documents et beauté des oeuvres."--P. [4] of cover
